title: Private installer: add KMS preflight checks (region/permissions/reachability) + clearer errors
author: Bruno Silva
release_notes: Private installer now validates KMS configuration during install/upgrade (endpoint/region, credentials/IAM permissions, key status) and emits actionable remediation steps instead of generic KMS failures.
body:
Context: We’ve had multiple Private deploy installs/upgrades where the control plane comes up but the first decrypt/encrypt in the data plane fails due to KMS misconfiguration (wrong region/endpoint, missing IAM permissions, disabled key, network egress issues). This PR adds an explicit KMS preflight stage to fail fast with actionable error messages and minimal risk. This is part of the KMS hardening/rotation project (ENG-4242, ENG-4217) and addresses patterns seen in SUP-18441.

What this changes: The installer now performs KMS checks during install and upgrade when a KMS provider is configured (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Checks are provider-aware and run before we apply manifests that depend on encryption. The preflight is designed to be safe (no persistent writes); it performs read-only identity/metadata checks and a short encrypt/decrypt round-trip against a random test plaintext in-memory.

Preflight checks (by provider): AWS KMS: (1) Validate key ARN format and region alignment vs configured region; (2) Resolve and call kms:DescribeKey and kms:GetKeyPolicy (when allowed) to confirm key exists and is Enabled; (3) Execute encrypt+decrypt with an ephemeral payload to prove permissions: kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey (if configured for envelope usage); (4) Detect common AccessDenied patterns and return the missing action(s) and principal ARN; (5) Detect endpoint failures (timeouts, NXDOMAIN, connection refused) and report probable network/VPC egress causes. GCP KMS: (1) Validate resource path (projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*); (2) Ensure location matches configured region mapping; (3) Call getCryptoKey and validate primary state is ENABLED; (4) Attempt encrypt/decrypt; (5) Map permission errors to roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter guidance plus service account identity. Azure Key Vault: (1) Validate vault URL and key name/version config; (2) Fetch key metadata and validate key is enabled; (3) Attempt wrapKey/unwrapKey or encrypt/decrypt depending on configured mode; (4) Map authorization failures to the expected Key Vault access policy / RBAC permissions.

User experience: Errors now include: provider, key identifier, detected region, the exact failing API call, request id (if available), and a “How to fix” block with the minimum required permissions and links to our Private KMS docs section (internal doc link referenced in installer output only when the operator has opted in to include help URLs). Example output for AWS: "KMS preflight failed: AccessDenied calling kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:1234:key/… as arn:aws:sts::1234:assumed-role/redwood-private-installer/… Required permissions: kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey (if envelope) on this key + allow kms:ViaService if restricted. Verify key policy allows this principal and the key is Enabled."

Safety/behavior: Preflight is opt-out via --skip-kms-preflight (intended only for breakglass/advanced debugging). Default is on for new installs and upgrades when KMS is configured. The preflight respects existing installer timeouts; each provider check has a bounded retry and a hard deadline (default 25s) so we don’t hang upgrades indefinitely.

Implementation notes: Added provider-specific clients behind a common interface to keep error mapping and output consistent. Introduced a small “diagnostics” package for structured preflight results (status, reason, remediation). Added a dry-run mode to print what would be checked without making calls (useful for restricted environments).

Files/areas changed (high-level): cmd/redwood-private-installer/main.go (wire preflight stage + flags); internal/preflight/kms/ (new provider adapters, shared interface, result formatter); internal/preflight/kms/aws.go, gcp.go, azure.go (provider checks); internal/config/kms.go (region validation + key id parsing); internal/ui/printer.go (improved error blocks); docs/installer/flags.md (document --skip-kms-preflight and --kms-preflight-timeout); test/ (unit tests for parsing and error mapping + integration-style stubs).

Illustrative snippet: Added standardized remediation formatting.

Before: "error: failed to initialize KMS client"
After: "KMS preflight failed (aws-kms): AccessDenied calling kms:DescribeKey (request_id=...) Key: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:... Detected region mismatch: configured=us-east-1 key=us-west-2 How to fix: set kms.region=us-west-2 OR update key ARN; ensure IAM policy grants kms:DescribeKey, kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt".

Commits: 1) preflight: introduce KMS checker interface and result model 2) aws: add DescribeKey + encrypt/decrypt roundtrip and error mapping 3) gcp/azure: implement preflight adapters 4) installer: add preflight stage, flags, and docs 5) tests: parsing + error mapping coverage

Testing: Unit tests for key parsing and error mapping; local manual tests against dev AWS key with (a) correct permissions (pass), (b) missing kms:Decrypt (fails with targeted message), (c) wrong region (fails with region mismatch), (d) disabled key (fails with key state). CI: lint, unit, cross-build.

Rollout/notes: This is intended to reduce time-to-diagnosis during Private installs and upgrades. Operators who rely on constrained network access may need to ensure KMS endpoints are reachable from the installer environment. The preflight does not modify keys or policies.

Review conversation summary: Hanae requested we ensure no persistent writes and that our test payload is never logged; updated to use fixed-length random bytes and redacted output. Marcus requested least-privilege guidance strings be accurate and not over-broad; updated remediation to list minimum actions per mode and note key policy requirements. Sean requested bounded timeouts and clear distinction between transient network errors vs auth; added per-call deadlines and categorized errors (network/auth/config/key-state).

Merge: Squash merged to main.
review_thread:
Hanae Suzuki: Can we confirm the preflight doesn’t create any persistent artifacts in customer KMS (e.g., new aliases, tags, or key versions)? Also please ensure the plaintext/ciphertext is never logged. Bruno Silva: Confirmed. Preflight only calls Describe/Get + encrypt/decrypt with an in-memory payload; no alias creation or tagging. I also redacted payload bytes in the diagnostic output and added a unit test to ensure we don’t print buffer contents.

Marcus Lin: The remediation text currently suggests kms:* in one place. We should avoid implying broad permissions; list the specific actions we require and clarify the key policy must allow the installer principal. Bruno Silva: Updated remediation templates to enumerate required actions (DescribeKey/Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey depending on envelope config) and added key-policy note. Removed the overly broad example.

Sean Gallagher: Please cap retries; upgrades should not hang for minutes if KMS endpoint is blackholed. Also can you differentiate DNS/timeout from AccessDenied so on-call can triage quickly. Bruno Silva: Added --kms-preflight-timeout (default 25s) with per-call deadlines, max 2 retries for transient failures, and error classification (network/auth/config/key-state). Output now starts with the classification tag.

Diego Santos: Nit: region mapping for GCP locations vs our deployment region labels—can we accept both "us-central1" and "us"? Bruno Silva: I kept strict matching to locations for the KMS resource, but I added a hint if the operator passes a broad label; we show the correct location string to use.

Approvals: Hanae Suzuki (approved), Marcus Lin (approved), Sean Gallagher (approved).
